Nicknamed "'''the Finnisher'''",{{cite web |last1=Kostecka |first1=Ryan |title="Staying Focused On What We Can Control" {{!}} The Jazz Welcome The Clippers To Utah For Round Three |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/staying-focused-on-what-we-can-control-the-jazz-welcome-the-clippers-to-utah-for-round-three |website=www.nba.com |access-date=5 December 2022 |language=en}} he is the son of Finnish basketball players [[Pekka Markkanen|Pekka]] and Riikka Markkanen, and the younger brother of [[Association football|footballer]] [[Eero Markkanen]]. Starting his career with [[HBA-Märsky]] in the Finnish second-tier league, Markkanen represented Finland at the [[FIBA U18 EuroBasket]] in [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2015]] and the [[FIBA U20 EuroBasket]] in [[2016 FIBA U20 European Championship|2016]], and was the top scorer in both tournaments. He moved to the United States and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] in the 2016–17 season, where he earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honours in his lone year with the team. He was selected seventh overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] before being included in a draft-night trade to the [[Chicago Bulls]] for [[Jimmy Butler]]. Following a stint with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Markkanen experienced a career resurgence in his first year with the Jazz, earning his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] selection and winning the [[NBA Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player Award]] in 2023. He also led Finland in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] tournament. After two successful seasons with the Jazz, Markkanen signed a five-year contract extension with the franchise. Markkanen was named the [[Finnish Sports Personality of the Year|Finnish Athlete of the Year]] in 2023, as the first basketball player ever to win the award.[https://yle.fi/a/74-20069011/64-3-202673 Vuoden urheilija on Lauri Markkanen!], [[Yle]], 11 January 2024[https://yle.fi/a/74-20069066 Lauri Markkanen on Vuoden urheilija! NBA-valmentaja pääsi opettelemaan heti suomea – äidiltä hulvaton tarina], [[Yle]], 11 January 2024 ==Early life and career== Markkanen was born in [[Vantaa]], but grew up in [[Jyväskylä]]. He played his junior years in the local team HoNsU ({{ill|Hongikon Nuorisoseuran Urheilijat|fi|Hongikon Nuorisoseuran Urheilijat (koripallo)}}).{{cite news|title= Koripallon poikkeuslahjakkuus Lauri Markkanen harjoitteli heittoja jopa ilman pakkasrajaa|url=http://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000002889803.html|work=Helsingin Sanomat|date=6 March 2016|language=fi-FI}} In 2014, Markkanen moved to [[Helsinki]] and joined Helsinki Basketball Academy. He played for the academy team [[HBA-Märsky]] in the [[Koripallon I-divisioona|Finnish second-tier league]] from 2014 to 2016. He attended the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp in 2015. ==College career== On 17 October 2015, Markkanen verbally committed to the NCAA Division I squad [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] prior to the 2016–17 season.{{cite news|title=UA basketball: Finnish big man Markkanen commits|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|date=17 October 2015|url=http://tucson.com/sports/basketball/college/wildcats/ua-basketball-finnish-big-man-markkanen-commits/article_e966bcd3-c48f-5d2d-9ff6-14c271e92a71.html}}{{cite news|title=Finnish forward Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|publisher=Sports Illustrated|author=Jeremy Woo|date=17 October 2015|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/10/17/arizona-wildcats-lauri-markkanen-commits-finland-sean-miller}}{{cite news|title=Finland's five-star forward Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|author=Sam Vecenie|work=CBS Sports|date=17 October 2015|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25343238/finlands-five-star-forward-lauri-markkanen-commits-to-arizona}} Lauri signed a letter of intent to Arizona on 11 November. ESPN.com reported that the seven-foot Finn was considered "a possible one-and-done candidate for the NBA draft."{{cite news|title=Finnish big man Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|work=ESPN.com|author=Jeff Borzello|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13908331/finnish-center-lauri-markkanen-commits-arizona-wildcats}} He became the first Wildcats player since [[Mike Bibby]] to wear the jersey number 10. In January 2017, ''[[SB Nation]]'' regarded him as "the best shooting 7-footer college basketball has ever seen".{{cite news|last1=O'Donnell|first1=Ricky|title=Lauri Markkanen is the best shooting 7-footer college basketball has ever seen|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/1/20/14336960/arizona-lauri-markkanen-shooting-nba-draft-2017|work=SBNation.com|date=20 January 2017}} Markkanen was selected to the third team All-American team by the [[Associated Press]], [[NBC Sports]], ''[[USA Today]]'', and the ''[[Sporting News]]'' on 6 March 2017.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/college-basketball-all-americans-2017-sporting-news-lonzo-ball-josh-hart-justin-jackson-frank-mason-caleb-swanigan/1tnhntha9fb3q1b468aho78tbp|title=Sporting News 2017 college basketball All-Americans|website=www.sportingnews.com|date=6 March 2017 }} He was a first team All-Pac-12 selection, as well as first team All-Pac-12 Freshman team and first team All-Pac-12 team in Associated Press. At the conclusion of his freshman season, Markkanen announced his intention to forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-freshman-lauri-markkanen-confirms-he-ll-leave-for/article_3db2a624-156a-11e7-931e-83d630618d4c.html|title=Arizona Wildcats freshman Lauri Markkanen confirms he'll leave for NBA |website=tucson.com|author=Bruce Pascoe|date=30 March 2017|access-date=30 March 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2021)=== Markkanen was drafted by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the seventh pick of the first round of the 2017 NBA draft. Markkanen missed the first 23 games of the season. He had a career-high 19 rebounds in a loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on 28 January. He also had 31 points and 18 rebounds in a win over Brooklyn on 8 February; a career-high 35 points along with 15 rebounds in a win over the [[Boston Celtics]] on 23 February; and 31 points and 17 rebounds in win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on 1 March. On 28 March, Markkanen was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing tests for his health problems,{{cite web |title=Lauri Markkanen Update |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/lauri-markkanen-update-0 |website=NBA.com |access-date=28 March 2019 |date=27 March 2019}} which he experienced in a 26 March game against the [[Toronto On 12 February 2026, the Jazz were fined $500,000 by the NBA for sitting out Markkanen and [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]].[https://yle.fi/a/74-20210052 NBA sai tarpeekseen Utah Jazzin touhusta – Lauri Markkasen seuralle jättisakot], [[Yle]], 13 February 2026 Markkanen played 42 games and averaged a career-high 26.7 points, 2.1 assists and 1 steal.[https://yle.fi/a/74-20221846 Lauri Markkanen teki kovaa jälkeä NBA:ssa, mutta kausi jäi torsoksi – nyt hän avaa Ylelle isoja odotuksiaan ensi kauteen], [[Yle]], 23 April 2026 ==National team career== [[File:Lauri Markkanen.jpg|thumb|Markkanen with Finland U20 in 2016.]] [[File:EuroBasket 2017 France vs Finland 01.jpg|thumb|left|170px|Markkanen in [[2017 Eurobasket]]]] ===Junior national team=== Markkanen made his international debut with the Finnish U-18 national team at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article102553812.html|title=Former KU forward Pekka Markkanen's son, Lauri, expected to excel at Arizona|last=Bedore|first=Gary|date=17 September 2016|work=The Kansas City Star|access-date=12 May 2017}} Markkanen averaged 18.2 points per game and was the top scorer in the tournament. He was the top scorer also in [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] tournament for Finland U20 with an average of 24.9 points per game and was named to the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web|title=All-Star Five - Lauri Markkanen is the top scorer! - FIBA U20 European Championship 2016 - FIBA U20 European Championship Division A 2016 - FIBA.com|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2016/videos/All-Star-Five-Lauri-Markkanen-is-the-top-scorer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006064447/http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2016/videos/All-Star-Five-Lauri-Markkanen-is-the-top-scorer|url-status=live|archive-date=6 October 2017|website=FIBA.com|access-date=24 January 2017}} ===Senior national team=== Markkanen played with the [[Finland men's national basketball team|Finland senior national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2017]], which was partly held in his home country. He led his team to the round of 16 by averaging 19.5 points and 5.7 rebounds over 6 games.{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Lauri-Markkanen|title=Lauri Markkanen Profile|publisher=[[EuroBasket 2017]]|access-date=28 October 2017}} He played his second EuroBasket tournament in [[EuroBasket 2022|2022]]. In the Round of 16, Markkanen scored 43 points to lead Finland to a 94–86 win over [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]], setting a new all-time record for a Finnish player at the EuroBasket.{{Cite web |title=Markkanen takeover: 43-point special sends Finland to the Quarter-Finals |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/markkanen-takeover-43-point-special-sends-finland-to-the-quarter-finals |access-date=2022-09-11 |website=FIBA.basketball}} The win also led to Finland's first quarterfinal appearance in 55 years, the last being in 1967. Finland eventually lost in the following quarterfinals to Spain 100–90. Markkanen averaged 27.9 points on 54.2 per cent shooting and eight rebounds over seven games.{{Cite web |title=Lauri MARKKANEN at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/player/Lauri-Markkanen |access-date=2022-09-14 |website=FIBA.basketball}} Markkanen was named in the Finnish national team roster to play [[2023 FIBA World Cup]]. In the tournament, he averaged 24.8 points and 8 rebounds over five games,[https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/196372/Lauri-Markkanen Lauri Markkanen], [[FIBA]] but after the losses in the group stage, Finland finished in 21st place out of 32 teams. On August 8, 2025, Markkanen scored a career-high 48 points, going 17-from-23 from the field, in a 105–62 friendly win over [[Belgium men's national basketball team|Belgium]] in the preparation for [[EuroBasket 2025]].{{Cite web |date=2025-08-08 |title=Unstoppable: Markkanen erupts for career-high 48 points |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/unstoppable-markkanen-errupts-for-career-high-48-points |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} He set a Finland national team record, surpassing his own previous record from 2022. At the [[EuroBasket 2025]], Markkanen averaged 23.1 points and 8.1 rebounds per game, leading Finland to a historic semi-final appearance. Finland ultimately finished 4th, making it the best result in the country's history. During the tournament, Markkanen surpassed 500 points scored in EuroBasket career, as the second Finnish player behind [[Timo
